experiment: 3-class head (real / diffusion-fake / GAN-fake) on the eta=0 features
question: does letting the head separate GAN fakes from diffusion fakes remove biggan's below-chance inversion (39.8% under scheme C)?
protocol: trained on the first half of each of the six test generators' features (36k; biggan is the only GAN class member), same backbone and hyperparameters; binary accuracy collapses the two fake classes
caveat: per-generator numbers below are computed over BOTH halves, i.e. they include the training half; the clean held-out figure is best_val_binary_acc (second halves only). Unlike the LOGO runs, every generator was seen in training here.
observations: biggan's inversion disappears: 39.8% (below chance) -> 63.4% binary / AP 0.68 once GAN-fake is its own class
the other non-SD generators also move above chance (57-61%) when they appear in training, consistent with the LOGO finding that presence in training is what matters
wukong drops from 78.5% (sdv1.4-trained model) to 57.4% here -- this run's training set contains no sdv1.4-scale SD data
clean held-out binary accuracy (val halves) is 54.3%, so absolute numbers remain modest; the result is directional (the inversion artefact is class-structure, not noise)
